checks: A maximizing sequence for perturbed support normals clusters in the old exposed face. Together with testing old exposed points this proves the one-sided support derivative.
The d facet intercepts along rays from the opposite vertex have first variations (k−v·p_l)/(h−u·q). Their product and the simplex height formula give the correct factor of facet area divided by |u|.

Homothety scales facet areas by r_i^(d−1). The aggregate right derivative is a positive common factor times a support-function inequality. Separation gives exactly the Minkowski membership and not individual facet contact.

The determinant and vertex formulas are smooth in normals and offsets near a nondegenerate orientation. Simultaneous right derivatives therefore add their one-facet contributions. Singleton terms vanish for d≥2 and interval orientations are constant for d=1.
The formula and necessity/sufficiency match ae6af582a4950210 §§3–4.

dependencies.hypotheses: Its common homothety model supplies the relative facet area scaling and the positive-radius versus singleton distinction for every orientation.
dependencies.review_status: Same-wave frozen input. Admission requires its separate independent approval.

overlap.comparison: One-body minimizers have individual facet-centroid contacts. Here several envelopes must share an orientation and the conclusion is an aggregate equivalence for all first derivatives, not individual contact.
The common active-offset representation for lifted simplex vertices addresses a different geometric condition and gives no weighted orientation derivative.

readability: The hypotheses and the proof use the same scope.

summary: The exact first-order derivative characterizes stationarity by the weighted aggregate exposed-face memberships.
